episode_title: How Executives Can Spot Burnout Before It Becomes a Health Crisis

real_qa.q: What are the early warning signs of burnout in high-functioning executives before health crisis occurs?
real_qa.r: Sleep deprivation is typically the first indicator, followed by physical symptoms like getting sick more often, longer recovery times, compromised immune system, or being prescribed new medications. Burnout happens because executives override the body's intelligent signals—fatigue, aches, and pain—by taking ibuprofen, drinking more coffee, or pushing through, and over time the body responds with increasingly severe consequences.
real_qa.requete: burnout warning signs executives before health crisis

real_qa.q: What does 'living the width of your life' mean according to Aneta Kuzma's philosophy?
real_qa.r: It means treating every single day as valuable by focusing on quality of relationships, health, contribution to the world, laughter, joy, and moments of awe, rather than just living through years without presence or memory. It's about being present enough to appreciate goodness available each day instead of always focusing on the next thing, which causes you to miss the present—your actual entire life.
real_qa.requete: living width of your life meaning Aneta Kuzma

real_qa.q: What practical daily routines can busy executives implement to manage stress and avoid burnout?
real_qa.r: Get morning sunlight with coffee or journaling, set daily intentions in positivity before checking email, use psychological sigh breath work (two inhales through belly to chest, then slow exhale, repeated three times) to reset the nervous system throughout the day, dim lights 60-90 minutes before sleep, and do one activity before bed that is only for you—not tied to work or roles—like reading, journaling, gratitude, prayer, or meditation.
real_qa.requete: stress management routines executives burnout prevention

real_qa.q: How did Aneta Kuzma transition from a 25-year banking career to starting her coaching business in January 2019?
real_qa.r: An MBA assignment requiring a 20-page life vision statement first prompted deep reflection about her desires. Later, health scares while burned out became a catalyst to hire an executive coach for six months while still working full time. She spent two years building her business from 5 p.m. to 9 p.m. and weekends before an October day when she had a visceral reaction to upcoming organizational expense cuts and decided it was time to launch full-time.
real_qa.requete: Aneta Kuzma transition banking to coaching business 2019

real_qa.q: What is the ikigai framework and how does it help professionals discover meaningful next chapters?
real_qa.r: Ikigai, a Japanese term referenced in Blue Zones research about Okinawa, examines the intersection of four elements: what you are good at, what you are passionate about, what the world needs, and what you can get paid for. That intersection reveals possible directions for meaningful work aligned with values, allowing professionals to use all previous skills and experience as gifts in a new chapter.
real_qa.requete: ikigai framework finding purpose career transition

guest.bio_context: Aneta spent 25 years in corporate banking before starting her own coaching and consulting business in January 2019. She works primarily with executives experiencing burnout despite external success, and creates wellness programs for organizations. She holds an MBA with a focus on emotional intelligence from a program that included work with Dr. Boyatzis, and hosts a podcast titled 'Living the Width of Your Life.'
